title: Invocation contract watchdog: schema + function-signature diffing for rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement an automated watchdog that compares invocation contracts (structured output shapes and function-call signatures) between current and candidate model variants during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. Scope: runtime diff detector that runs on shadow traffic, a light-weight runtime agent that flags incompatible deltas, end-to-end test harness for simulated tool-calls, and an auto-rollback trigger tied to delta severity and customer-impact scoring.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime agent ingests a canonical schema and live invocation telemetry and emits structured diff events to the rollout controller
System classifies diffs into compatibility tiers (safe, warned, breaking) with documented heuristics
Shadow validation runs for a candidate model produce an aggregated delta report within 2 minutes for 1k requests
Auto-rollback policy can be configured by route (percent mismatch threshold + severity) and triggers a rollback in < 60s when exceeded
Unit/integration tests cover signature diffing for: added optional fields, removed required fields, argument type changes, and function name renames
tasks: Design runtime diff event schema and proto for contract deltas
Implement lightweight diffing library (protobuf/JSON Schema + heuristics) in runtime (Go) and SDK shim (Python/TS)
Add shadow traffic sampling and aggregator to rollout controller
Wire diff events into Console UI: per-route compatibility heatmap
Create e2e harness to replay production traces against candidate models
Define auto-rollback config surface and implement enforcement in rollout pipeline
Add telemetry (counts, severity distribution, example payloads) to observability stack
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design. Agreed scope: runtime detector + controller integration; console mockups deferred to follow-up
2026-02-27: Prototype diff lib implemented in Go (proof: detects removed required keys + arg-type widening). PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1129
2026-03-03: Shadow aggregator sketch reviewed. Concern raised about privacy of example payloads; decided to mask PII and only store context hashes

2026-03-07: Integration test harness created using synthetic traces. Candidate model with renamed function produced 'breaking' tier. Observed false positives for added optional fields; tuned heuristics to ignore additive optional fields by default
2026-03-11: Telemetry pipeline wired to metrics pipeline (internal: grafana/dashboards). Initial dashboard shows 0.3% breaking diffs on internal canary (expected)
2026-03-12: Began work on auto-rollback action wiring; first smoke test succeeded in staging (rollback completed in 37s)
decisions: Only treat removal of required fields, function name changes, and type narrowing as 'breaking' by default
Additive optional fields are 'safe' unless downstream strict-typed clients are opted-in to strict validation
Telemetry examples stored as redacted JSON + context-hash to balance triage speed and privacy
Auto-rollback will require two signals: (1) severity-weighted mismatch rate over window, and (2) customer-impact flag or route tag to avoid noisy rollbacks on low-impact routes
tradeoffs: Aggressive detection reduces risk of silent regressions but increases false positives and blocking of benign model variants
Storing example payloads helps debugging but increases PII risk; mitigated with redaction and retention limits
Running diffing synchronously increases per-request overhead; chose asynchronous shadow-path with aggregation for production rollouts
test_plan: Integration: replay 10k production trace snippets against older/newer model families in staging
Chaos: inject synthetic function-call renames during A/B route at 5% traffic and assert rollback triggers
Performance: measure aggregator latency at 1k rps shadowing and ensure aggregation < 2 minutes
monitoring: Alert: contract_delta_breaking_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m on customer-facing route => Pager to SRE
Dashboard: per-route heatmap, top-20 example redacted payloads, rolling window severity histogram
runbook: 2) Triage dashboard link in alert (includes redacted examples + last diff snapshots)
3) If confirmed breaking: trigger immediate rollback via rollout controller (automated if auto-rollback enabled)
4) Post-mortem: collect failing examples and open ENG ticket for model-owner to patch prompt/response contract
5) If false-positive: escalate to infra to adjust heuristics and tag route as 'strict-validation-exempt' if appropriate
notes: Follow-up PI: add SDK validation helpers for downstream clients to opt-in strict-contract enforcement
Consider adding ML-based fuzzy matching for argument semantics in a later iteration
Design to support JSON Schema and protobuf descriptors in the long term
